inputs.text: Developments inside Nigeria's ruling All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections show how political parties have become closed clubs serving only the wealthy elite, completely abandoning any role in supporting the broader population. This reveals entrenched structural inequalities where those at the top consolidate power and resources for themselves, leaving ordinary citizens and vulnerable groups pushed to the margins. The root causes lie in historical patterns of elite capture and institutional failures that prioritize the rich over social justice, not some rejection of traditions. Without serious reforms to dismantle these power imbalances and protect marginalized communities from ongoing economic exclusion, the pattern of inequality will only deepen.
